Let me analyze this conflict.

Axis: applicant
- Register: "Datalogic Scanning, Inc."
- Document: "Datalogic ADC, Inc."

Are these the same entity? Datalogic ADC, Inc. and Datalogic Scanning, Inc. — Datalogic ADC is the division of Datalogic group handling Automatic Data Capture, which includes scanning products. Historically, Datalogic Scanning, Inc. was renamed/reorganized into Datalogic ADC, Inc. around 2007-2008. The certificate document is the legal instrument from 2013, saying "Datalogic ADC, Inc." The register says "Datalogic Scanning, Inc."

Is this a name change (same legal entity, different names over time) or genuinely different names? Datalogic Scanning, Inc. was indeed a US entity that later became Datalogic ADC, Inc. So arguably same corporate lineage. But at the time of the certificate (2013), the legal name on the certificate is "Datalogic ADC, Inc." The register's value "Datalogic Scanning, Inc." might come from an older record or an OIML database entry.

The rules: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)." "Spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity."

"Datalogic Scanning, Inc." vs "Datalogic ADC, Inc." — "Scanning" vs "ADC" is not spelling drift; it's a different name. These are two distinct registered names (one was renamed to the other, but they're not just spelling variants). So the verdict is different-entity, with best_value = document's "Datalogic ADC, Inc." since the certificate is the legal instrument.

Alternatively, one could argue same-entity due to corporate renaming. But the fusion rules don't have a "renamed" category; different names that are not spelling drift = different-entity. The certificate is the legal instrument, so the document value wins.
